Note: Transparent scoring for Quick Scan. Edit freely. Points per unique rule = Weight x (1 + log10(hits)), capped per severity. A flag adds its points once when a rule of severity low or higher matches its pattern.

Flags.Reason: Event logs were cleared or auditing was changed. Attackers do this to hide their tracks.
Antivirus protection was turned off or weakened.
Signs of credential theft (LSASS, Mimikatz style, DCSync, Kerberoasting or hash/ticket reuse).
Behaviour typical of ransomware preparation (shadow copies or recovery options removed).
Names of well-known attack frameworks or remote-execution tools appear in the findings.
Encoded, obfuscated or download-and-run PowerShell was seen.
A new or suspicious service, scheduled task, autorun or WMI subscription was created.
A new account was created or added to an administrator group.
A source that failed to log on many times later logged on successfully (possible password guessing that worked).

Verdicts.Name: No rule matched
Verdicts.Text: None of the bundled rules matched these logs. This does not prove the machine is clean: the logs may be incomplete, short, or missing the sources that matter (see Blind spots).

Verdicts.Name: A few findings
Verdicts.Text: Some rule matches. Most are often normal activity, but review the top findings.

Verdicts.Name: Needs attention
Verdicts.Text: Several suspicious findings. Treat as a lead and verify the top findings and the accounts and hosts involved.

Verdicts.Name: Likely malicious
Verdicts.Text: Many serious findings together. Behave as if there is an incident: preserve evidence first, then investigate the incident window.

Verdicts.Name: Serious indicators
Verdicts.Text: Strong, multiple indicators of attacker activity. Treat as an incident and preserve evidence before changing anything.
